vulnerabilities.description: The `/api/monitor` endpoint at `routes.py:20-44` has no authentication mechanism. It accepts a `command` parameter in a POST request and, if the command equals `secret_phrase` (line 28), returns the flag. There is no session validation, no API key, no CSRF token, and no rate limiting. Combined with VULN-001 (which leaks the secret_phrase), any unauthenticated attacker can retrieve the flag by sending a single POST request.

vulnerabilities.description: The frontend JavaScript in `main.js:45` performs a client-side check that only allows commands present in `availableOptions[currentStep]` or `availableOptions['secret']` to be sent to the `/api/monitor` endpoint. However, the backend at `routes.py:20-44` does NOT perform any equivalent validation. The backend accepts ANY command value and only checks if it equals `secret_phrase` (line 28) or tries to look it up in `answers[currentStep]` (line 30). This means an attacker can bypass the frontend entirely and send arbitrary commands directly to the API, including the secret_phrase needed to get the flag.
vulnerabilities.data_flow: Frontend: main.js:45 validates command against whitelist → main.js:46 sends POST to /api/monitor → Backend: routes.py:24 extracts command → routes.py:28 checks if command == secret_phrase → returns flag. The backend has NO whitelist validation, so direct API calls bypass the frontend check entirely.
